actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species is known from the lowland forests of the Guianas and adjacent Brazil in the states of Amapá (at Serra do Tumucumaque and Serra do Navio) and Pará (municipality of Oriximiná and Estação Ecológica Grão Pará). It occurs up to 600 m asl.
documentation.population: It is locally common in French Guiana (Lescure and Marty 2001). Elsewhere it is common but patchily distributed. The population is presumed to be stable based on the status of its habitat and lack of threats.
documentation.habitats: It inhabits the forest floor in lowland tropical rainforest. Its eggs are laid out of water, and then the tadpoles are carried by the males to puddles or tree holes where they develop further.
documentation.threats: Localized habitat loss driven by agriculture and logging are threats to the species' habitat. Gaucher and MacCulloch (2010) consider illegal collecting for the pet trade a major threat. Although this species may be potentially threatened by trade, it is currently not possible to determine whether or not individuals being traded are captive-bred or wild-caught (or, if they are wild-caught, whether or not this species is being over-harvested).
documentation.measures:
Conservation Actions In-Place
This species occurs in a few protected areas throughout its range. It breeds easily in captivity and is found in zoos around the world.

Research Needed
Further research on this species' distribution, population size and trends is recommended, as are studies to determine the origin of individuals found in the international pet trade, and whether or not this species is being over-harvested.
documentation.use_trade:
This species is a widely traded frog. Gorzula (1996) provides an overview and discussion of the trade in Dendrobatidae, from which it is clear that Dendrobates tinctorius is one of the four most traded species. Exports originate mostly from Suriname and to a lesser degree from Guyana, with both countries having a voluntary export quota. Historically and at present, no captive bred specimens originate from Suriname; all specimens exported are wild-caught. In 2013 Suriname exceeded its export quota for this species considerably (CITES 2015).

Brazil and French Guiana prohibit the export of specimens. Despite this, a number of D. tinctorius morphs, only known from Brazil, have been in the terrarium trade for years. These specimens were probably smuggled out of Brazil either directly to Europe, or via Suriname to Europe. In French Guiana, several shipments containing this species have been intercepted in Cayenne (Marty and Vacher 2013).
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution and presumed large and stable population.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: We follow Wollenberg et al. (2006) in considering Dendrobates azureus as a junior synonym of this species. Hoogmoed (2019) discussed nominal Dendrobates azureus and suggested reasons for doubting its synonymy.
